region: East and Southern Africa, Horn interior, Madagascar and Comoros

polities.name: Ethiopian Empire
polities.note: Highland Christian core. Itinerant royal camps before 1636; Gondar 1636-1855; Debre Tabor/Magdala/Mekelle under Tewodros/Yohannes; Addis Ababa from 1886. 1529-1543 largely overrun by Adal. 1769-1855 Zemene Mesafint: emperor nominal, regional lords (listed separately) ruled. Tributary margins (Hadiya, Bale, Dawaro, Ennarea) listed separately. Menelik's conquests 1880-1900 roughly doubled the area.

polities.name: Adal Sultanate
polities.note: Walashma successor of Ifat. Seat Dakkar until 1520, then Harar. Under Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim (Gragn) 1529-1543 it occupied most of the Ethiopian highlands. Weakened by Oromo migrations; court moved to Aussa 1577 (see Imamate of Aussa).

polities.name: Ifat Sultanate
polities.note: Tributary to Ethiopia from 1332; destroyed by Yeshaq I in 1415, heirs fled to found Adal.

polities.name: Hadiya Sultanate
polities.note: Muslim tributary state of the Ethiopian Empire south of the Awash; overrun in the Oromo migrations c.1560-1570.

polities.name: Sultanate of Bale
polities.note: Muslim tributary of Ethiopia; occupied by Arsi Oromo c.1560.

polities.name: Sultanate of Dawaro
polities.note: Between Hararghe and Bale; Ethiopian tributary, absorbed by Oromo migrations.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ennarea
polities.note: Gonga kingdom, gold trade; Ethiopian tributary. Overrun by Macha Oromo c.1700-1710; successor Oromo state Limmu-Ennarea.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kaffa
polities.note: Gonga highland kingdom; Bonga later main town. Conquered by Menelik II 1897.

polities.name: Kingdom of Jimma
polities.note: Largest of the Gibe Oromo kingdoms; autonomous tributary of Ethiopia 1884-1932.

polities.name: Kingdom of Limmu-Ennarea
polities.note: Gibe Oromo kingdom (Abba Bagibo); tributary to Shewa/Ethiopia 1880s, annexed 1891.

polities.name: Kingdom of Gera
polities.note: Gibe Oromo kingdom; annexed by Ethiopia 1887.

polities.name: Kingdom of Gomma
polities.note: Gibe Oromo kingdom, early Islamized; annexed by Ethiopia 1886.

polities.name: Kingdom of Guma
polities.note: Gibe Oromo kingdom (Wikipedia: c.1770); conquered by Menelik II 1885; resistance under Firisa until 1901/02.

polities.name: Kingdom of Welayta
polities.note: Omotic kingdom (Tigre dynasty from c.1700); conquered by Menelik 1894 (King Tona).

polities.name: Kingdom of Janjero
polities.note: Small Omotic kingdom on the Omo/Gibe; tributary to Jimma, annexed by Ethiopia 1894.

polities.name: Kingdom of Dawro
polities.note: Omotic kingdom of Kullo west of the Omo; famous stone walls (Halala Kella); conquered by Menelik 1891.

polities.name: Kambaata kingdom
polities.note: Small Cushitic monarchy on Mount Hambaricho; annexed by Ethiopia 1890s.

polities.name: Sidama clans
polities.note: Clan-based Sidama polities with mote (chiefs) east of Lake Awasa; conquered by Menelik 1893.

polities.name: Gurage (Sebat Bet)
polities.note: Loose confederation of seven Gurage houses; overrun by Shewa 1875-1889.

polities.name: Medri Bahri
polities.note: Eritrean highland realm under the Bahr Negash; Ethiopian vassal, at times Ottoman-allied; absorbed by Yohannes IV / Egypt-Italy struggles by 1879-1890.

polities.name: Habesh Eyalet
polities.note: Ottoman Red Sea littoral (Massawa, Arkiko, Suakin); in practice run by the Balaw Naibs of Arkiko; passed to Egypt 1865-1872, Italian Massawa 1885.

polities.name: Kingdom of Shewa
polities.note: Autonomous Amhara kingdom (Negasi Krestos to Menelik); seats Doqaqit, Ankober, Angolalla, Entoto. Expanded south from 1870s; merged into empire when Menelik became emperor 1889.

polities.name: Yejju dynasty of Begemder
polities.note: Yejju Oromo Ras-regents (Ali I, Gugsa, Ali II) dominating the emperor at Gondar from Debre Tabor; ended by Tewodros at Ayshal 1853.

polities.name: Gojjam
polities.note: Autonomous province/kingdom within the Ethiopian Empire (Ras/Negus Tekle Haymanot 1881). Draw on top of Ethiopia in 1769-1855 and 1881-1901.

polities.name: Tigray (principality)
polities.note: Autonomous northern province under Ras Mikael Sehul, Wolde Selassie, Sabagadis, Wube; seat Adwa, Antalo; Yohannes IV ruled from Mekelle 1872-1889.

polities.name: Wollo (Wara Himano)
polities.note: Muslim Oromo dynasty ruling Wollo highlands; brought under Shewa/empire by 1876.

polities.name: Borana Oromo
polities.note: Gada-governed pastoral confederation of the southern plateau; assembly at Gumi Gayo. Incorporated by Ethiopia 1890s.

polities.name: Tulama Oromo
polities.note: Borana-branch Oromo confederation of central Shewa; gada centre at Odaa Nabee; subdued by Shewa 1840s-1886.

polities.name: Macha Oromo
polities.note: Western Oromo; from c.1800 crystallized into Gibe kingdoms (listed separately) and Leqa Nekemte/Qellem states. Subdued by Shewa 1880s.

polities.name: Leqa Nekemte
polities.note: Oromo state of Moroda Bakare; submitted peacefully to Menelik 1882, autonomous to 1930s.

polities.name: Arsi Oromo
polities.note: Barentu-branch Oromo of the Arsi-Bale plateau; conquered by Shewa 1882-1886.

polities.name: Afran Qallo Oromo
polities.note: Eastern Oromo (Ittu, Anniya, Nole, Ala, Jarso, Babile) of the Harar highlands around the city of Harar; Ethiopian conquest 1887.

polities.name: Raya and Azebo Oromo
polities.note: Northernmost Oromo on the Tigray-Wollo escarpment; autonomous until Yohannes/Menelik.

polities.name: Guji Oromo
polities.note: Gada-governed Oromo south of Sidama; conquered 1895.

polities.name: Emirate of Harar
polities.note: City-state emirate (Ali ibn Daud dynasty) surrounded by Oromo; Egyptian occupation 1875-1885; taken by Menelik at Chelenqo 1887.

polities.name: Imamate of Aussa
polities.note: Rump of Adal moved to the Aussa oasis by Imam Muhammad Jasa 1577; collapsed 1672 under Afar pressure.

polities.name: Sultanate of Aussa
polities.note: Leading Afar sultanate on the lower Awash (Mudaito dynasty, Kedafu). Nominal Ethiopian suzerainty from 1890s.

polities.name: Sultanate of Tadjoura
polities.note: Afar coastal sultanate; French protectorate 1884, part of French Somaliland (still exists ceremonially).

polities.name: Sultanate of Rahayta
polities.note: Afar sultanate at Bab el-Mandeb (Dankali coast); Italian protectorate 1880s, Eritrea.

polities.name: Sultanate of Gobaad
polities.note: Small Afar sultanate (Dardar/Adaali) in southwest Djibouti; under French protection from 1884. Dates poorly documented.

polities.name: Ajuran Sultanate
polities.note: Hydraulic state of the Shabelle-Juba interior and Benadir hinterland; Mogadishu, Merca, Barawa as tributary ports. Collapsed late 17th c.; successors Geledi and Hiraab.

polities.name: Sultanate of Mogadishu
polities.note: Benadir port sultanate (Fakhr ad-Din then Muzaffar dynasty); Ajuran vassal from 16th c.; later under Geledi/Hiraab influence and Omani/Zanzibari suzerainty (Zanzibar 1840s-1892, Italian lease 1892).

polities.name: Geledi Sultanate
polities.note: Successor of Ajuran in the lower Shabelle; at its height (Yusuf Mahamud Ibrahim, 1840s) controlled Benadir trade routes. Italian protectorate 1908/1910.

polities.name: Hiraab Imamate
polities.note: Hawiye (Hiraab) imamate that threw off Ajuran rule in the late 17th c.; Wikipedia gives Mogadishu as capital, with the Harardhere/El Dhere coast as its northern sphere. Ended 1889 (Italian treaties). Overlaps Sultanate of Mogadishu and Geledi spheres.

polities.name: Majeerteen Sultanate
polities.note: Northeast horn (Bari); Boqor Osman Mahamuud; seat Bargal/Alula. Italian protectorate 1889, conquered 1927.

polities.name: Sultanate of Hobyo
polities.note: Founded by Yusuf Ali Kenadid; Italian protectorate 1888; annexed 1925.

polities.name: Warsangali Sultanate
polities.note: Maakhir coast and Cal Madow; seat Durduri then Las Khorey (c.1740). British protectorate 1886.

polities.name: Isaaq Sultanate
polities.note: Clan sultanate of the Isaaq (Guled dynasty) in northwest Somalia, controlling Berbera trade; Habr Yunis split off 1769. British Somaliland protectorate 1884-87.

polities.name: Habr Yunis Sultanate
polities.note: Isaaq branch sultanate around Burao and the Haud (first seat Toyo); British protectorate from 1884/86.

polities.name: Gadabuursi Ugaasate
polities.note: Ugaas-led Dir clan polity west of the Isaaq, toward Zeila and Harar.

polities.name: Ogaden clans
polities.note: Darod pastoral clans of the Ogaden plateau without a single state; partly tributary to Harar/Adal; Ethiopian raids from 1890s.

polities.name: Dervish State
polities.note: Mohammed Abdullah Hassan's state in the Nugaal and Haud; forts at Taleh from 1913; destroyed by British air campaign 1920.

polities.name: Funj Sultanate
polities.note: Gezira core with vassal meks along the Nile (Abdallab, Ja'aliyin, Dongola, Fazughli). Kordofan contested with Darfur. Effective power under Hamaj regents after 1762. Conquered by Egypt 1821.

polities.name: Abdallab
polities.note: Arab dynasty ruling the northern Funj realm as viceroys (manjil); seat Qarri then Halfaya.

polities.name: Kingdom of Alodia
polities.note: Last Christian Nubian kingdom; by 1400 fragmented and in decline; destroyed by Funj/Abdallab c.1504.

polities.name: Kingdom of Dotawo
polities.note: Rump Christian Nubian kingdom of Lower Nubia after Makuria's collapse; last attested 1484.

polities.name: Kingdom of Dongola
polities.note: Funj vassal kingdom of the Dongola reach; Shaigiya pressure from late 17th c.; Mamluk refugees 1812; Egyptian conquest 1820.

polities.name: Shaigiya confederation
polities.note: Arab tribal confederation that broke away from the Funj c.1690 and dominated the Nile bend; defeated by Egypt at Korti 1820.

polities.name: Ja'aliyin of Shendi
polities.note: Ja'aliyin meks of Shendi and Metemma, Funj vassals; Mek Nimr burned Ismail Pasha 1822.

polities.name: Fazughli
polities.note: Funj vassal on the upper Blue Nile gold district (Bertha lands).

polities.name: Bela Shangul
polities.note: Watawit Arab-Bertha sheikhdoms (Khojali al-Hasan) on the Sudan-Ethiopia border; Egyptian, Mahdist then Ethiopian (1898) overlordship.

polities.name: Sultanate of Darfur
polities.note: Keira Fur dynasty; Jebel Marra origin, El Fasher fixed capital 1791. Held Kordofan 1785-1821. Conquered by Zubayr/Egypt 1874; restored under Ali Dinar 1898-1916.

polities.name: Musabba'at Sultanate
polities.note: Fur-related dynasty ruling Kordofan between Funj and Darfur; conquered by Darfur 1785.

polities.name: Kingdom of Taqali
polities.note: Muslim kingdom in the northeastern Nuba Mountains (oral tradition dates founding to the 16th c.). Tributary to Funj/Darfur/Egypt; later a native administration until 1969. 'to' marks end of real independence (Mahdist period).

polities.name: Shilluk Kingdom
polities.note: Reth-led Luo kingdom on the west bank of the White Nile; raided as far north as Aba Island in the 17th c.; seat at Fashoda from c.1700. Egyptian rule from 1861 (kingship continues).

polities.name: Dinka
polities.note: Acephalous pastoral nation of numerous sections (Rek, Agar, Bor, Padang, Ngok); no central ruler. Fills Bahr el Ghazal and Upper Nile floodplains.

polities.name: Nuer
polities.note: Acephalous pastoral nation; expanded east across the Sobat toward Ethiopia in the 19th c. (extent shown is 19th-c.).

polities.name: Anuak kingdom
polities.note: Luo-speaking villages with a rotating noble kingship (emblem-holder at Otalo) on the Baro/Pibor rivers.

polities.name: Masalit Sultanate
polities.note: Unified under Hajjam Hasab Allah 1874 between Wadai and Darfur; Mahdist invasion 1895; defeated by Ali Dinar 1903, Darfuri vassal from 1908 under Taj al-Din; independent again 1916-1922 under Bahr al-Din; joined Anglo-Egyptian Sudan 1922.

polities.name: Beja tribes
polities.note: Pastoral Beja confederacies of the Red Sea Hills; Beni Amer under Funj diglal; Suakin port Ottoman. Osman Digna's Mahdist base 1883-1891.

polities.name: Turco-Egyptian Sudan
polities.note: Khedivate of Egypt's Sudan provinces; seat Wad Madani then Khartoum (1830s). Expanded into Equatoria (1869-) and Darfur (1874). Fell to the Mahdi 1885.

polities.name: Mahdist State
polities.note: Muhammad Ahmad al-Mahdi and the Khalifa Abdallahi; destroyed at Omdurman 1898 (Anglo-Egyptian Sudan).

polities.name: Kingdom of Buganda
polities.note: Kabaka capitals moved each reign within Kyadondo/Busiro; expanded from 3 core counties at Bunyoro's expense 17th-19th c. British protectorate 1894.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bunyoro
polities.note: Babito Luo dynasty succeeding the legendary Chwezi Kitara c.1500; the dominant lakes power in the 16th-17th c., later lost Toro (1830), Kooki and counties to Buganda. Kabalega resisted British until 1899.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ankole
polities.note: Hinda dynasty Bahima kingdom; core Isingiro-Rwampara, absorbed Mpororo, Igara, Buhweju fragments in the 19th c. British 1901 (Ankole Agreement).

polities.name: Kingdom of Toro
polities.note: Broke from Bunyoro under Kaboyo Olimi I c.1830; reconquered by Kabalega 1876-1891, restored by the British.

polities.name: Kingdom of Karagwe
polities.note: Hinda kingdom west of Lake Victoria; height under Rumanyika (1855-1878); German East Africa from 1890.

polities.name: Kingdom of Rwanda
polities.note: Nyiginya dynasty; royal residences itinerant until Nyanza (1899). Small core in Nduga/Buganza until 17th-18th c.; Kigeli IV Rwabugiri (1853-1895) reached near-modern borders. German protectorate 1897.

polities.name: Kingdom of Burundi
polities.note: Founded by Ntare I Rushatsi c.1680; expanded greatly under Ntare IV Rugamba (c.1795-1850). Mwami Mwezi Gisabo resisted Germany until 1903.

polities.name: Busoga principalities
polities.note: About a dozen small Lwo-derived principalities (Bugabula, Bulamogi, Luuka, Bugweri, Bukooli, Kigulu, Busiki etc.), tributary to Buganda in the 19th c.; united under a Kyabazinga 1906.

polities.name: Bugabula
polities.note: Largest Busoga principality (Gabula dynasty).

polities.name: Bulamogi
polities.note: Northern Busoga principality (Zibondo dynasty).

polities.name: Kingdom of Mpororo
polities.note: Short-lived Bahima kingdom between Ankole and Rwanda; fragmented into Igara, Rujumbura, Kajara etc.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ndorwa
polities.note: Hima kingdom on the Rwanda-Uganda border; destroyed by Rwanda in the 18th c.

polities.name: Kooki
polities.note: Small Babito offshoot kingdom west of Lake Victoria; tributary to Buganda from early 19th c., annexed 1896.

polities.name: Buhweju
polities.note: Small highland kingdom absorbed into Ankole 1901.

polities.name: Kiziba
polities.note: Bito-dynasty Haya kingdom north of Bukoba; German East Africa 1890.

polities.name: Kyamutwara
polities.note: Hinda Haya kingdom (split into Kyamutwara and Kianja/Maruku in the 19th c.).

polities.name: Ihangiro
polities.note: Southern Haya kingdom.

polities.name: Buzinza
polities.note: Hinda kingdoms (Rusubi, Busindi) southwest of Lake Victoria.

polities.name: Kingdom of Gisaka
polities.note: Eastern Rwandan kingdom, annexed by Rwanda under Mutara II c.1852.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bugesera
polities.note: Hima kingdom around Lakes Cyohoha; partitioned by Rwanda and Burundi c.1795.

polities.name: Buha kingdoms
polities.note: Six small Ha kingdoms (Heru, Buyungu, Muhambwe, Ruguru, Bushingo, Ujiji-Buhinga) east of Lake Tanganyika.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ukerewe
polities.note: Island kingdom of the Kerebe (Silanga dynasty) in Lake Victoria.

polities.name: Acholi chiefdoms
polities.note: Some 60 small Luo rwot-led chiefdoms (Payira the largest); British 1890s-1910s.

polities.name: Alur chiefdoms
polities.note: Luo chiefdoms northwest of Lake Albert, spanning the Uganda-Congo border.

polities.name: Lango
polities.note: Acephalous Lango clans north of Lake Kyoga.

polities.name: Iteso
polities.note: Ateker pastoral-agricultural people of Teso; conquered by Kakungulu for the British 1899-1904.

polities.name: Karamojong
polities.note: Ateker pastoral nation of northeast Uganda.

polities.name: Turkana
polities.note: Ateker pastoral nation west of Lake Turkana; expanded east in the 19th c.

polities.name: Wanga Kingdom
polities.note: Luhya kingdom under the Nabongo (Shiundu, Mumia); British ally from 1883, absorbed into Kenya Colony.

polities.name: Kenya Luo
polities.note: Clan-territories (oganda) of the Nilotic Luo around the Winam Gulf.

polities.name: Nandi
polities.note: Kalenjin nation led by the Orkoiyot (Koitalel arap Samoei), resisted British until 1905.

polities.name: Kipsigis
polities.note: Kalenjin nation south of the Nandi.

polities.name: Maasai
polities.note: Pastoral sections (iloshon) of the Rift Valley under laibon ritual leaders; height mid-19th c.; weakened by rinderpest 1890s and British treaties 1904/1911.

polities.name: Samburu
polities.note: Maa-speaking pastoralists north of Laikipia.

polities.name: Kikuyu
polities.note: Acephalous ridge-based clans governed by age-grade councils (kiama) on the slopes of Mount Kenya and the Aberdares.

polities.name: Kamba
polities.note: Caravan-trading people of Ukambani; dominated ivory trade to Mombasa in the 18th-19th c.

polities.name: Meru
polities.note: Njuri Ncheke-governed sections northeast of Mount Kenya.

polities.name: Mijikenda
polities.note: Nine peoples living in fortified kaya settlements behind the Kenya coast; allied with Mombasa (Mazrui).

polities.name: Kilwa Sultanate
polities.note: Mahdali dynasty; dominated the southern Swahili coast and the Sofala gold trade in the 14th-15th c. Sacked by Portugal 1505 (fort until 1512); declining; Omani overlordship from 1784/85.

polities.name: Sofala sheikhdom
polities.note: Gold port at the end of the Zimbabwe-plateau trade, tributary to Kilwa; Portuguese fort 1505.

polities.name: Mombasa
polities.note: Shirazi sultans to 1593 (sacked 1505, 1528, 1589); Portuguese Fort Jesus 1593-1698 with Malindi dynasty as puppet sheikhs; Omani governors from 1698, autonomous under the Mazrui 1741-1837 (incl. Pemba); taken by Zanzibar 1837.

polities.name: Malindi
polities.note: Rival of Mombasa and Portuguese ally (Vasco da Gama 1498); its ruling house moved to Mombasa in 1593; later a Zanzibari town.

polities.name: Pate Sultanate
polities.note: Nabahani sultanate of the Lamu archipelago (Pate, Siyu, Faza); regional power in the 17th-18th c.; lost Lamu at Shela 1813; Nabahani retreated to Witu 1858; Zanzibari control from 1860s.

polities.name: Lamu
polities.note: Swahili city-state, often tributary to Pate; sought Omani protection after the Battle of Shela 1813.

polities.name: Witu Sultanate
polities.note: Founded by exiled Nabahani of Pate; German protectorate 1885-1890, British (IBEA) 1890.

polities.name: Barawa
polities.note: Benadir port city-state; tributary to Ajuran, sacked by Portugal 1506, later Geledi/Omani-Zanzibari influence; Italian 1892.

polities.name: Vumba Kuu
polities.note: Small Swahili-Segeju diwanate on the southern Kenya coast.

polities.name: Sultanate of Zanzibar
polities.note: Omani governorate of the East African coast from the fall of Fort Jesus (1698); Sayyid Said moved his court to Zanzibar 1840; separate sultanate 1856. Extent = islands plus a ~20 km coastal strip from Lamu to the Rovuma (1840-1886), with caravan influence inland. British protectorate 1890.

polities.name: Portuguese Mozambique
polities.note: Before 1890 only coastal forts (Sofala, Mozambique Island, Quelimane, Inhambane, Lourenço Marques) and the Zambezi corridor (Sena, Tete, Zumbo) with prazo estates; interior held by African states. Colony borders fixed 1891; capital Lourenço Marques 1898. Pre-1890 phase polygon is the Zambezi corridor plus Sofala coast; Mozambique Island, Quelimane, Inhambane and Lourenço Marques are point stations outside it.

polities.name: Angoche Sultanate
polities.note: Swahili-Makua sultanate; slave-trade power in the 19th c. under Musa Mohamad Sahib (Mussa Quanto) with Makua alliances; conquered by Portugal 1910.

polities.name: Sancul
polities.note: Swahili sheikhdom on the mainland south of Mozambique Island, nominal Portuguese vassal.

polities.name: Quitangonha
polities.note: Swahili sheikhdom north of Mozambique Island; slave-trading.

polities.name: Makua chiefdoms
polities.note: Many Makua-Lomwe chiefdoms (mwene) of northern Mozambique with shifting paramountcies; allied with or raiding the coastal sheikhdoms; pacified by Portugal 1896-1913.

polities.name: Makonde
polities.note: Acephalous plateau villages on both sides of the Rovuma.

polities.name: Sultanate of Ndzuwani
polities.note: Shirazi sultanate (capital Domoni, then Mutsamudu); often claimed overlordship of Mayotte and Mohéli; French protectorate 1886, annexed 1912.

polities.name: Sultanate of Mwali
polities.note: Established by the Merina exile Ramanetaka (Abderremane) c.1830; earlier under Anjouan. French protectorate 1886.

polities.name: Ngazidja sultanates
polities.note: Seven to eleven rival sultanates on Grande Comore; a Sultan Tibe (paramount) title passed between Bambao and Itsandra. Unified under Said Ali of Bambao with French protection 1886.

polities.name: Sultanate of Maore
polities.note: Shirazi sultanate (capital Tsingoni); seized by the Sakalava Andriantsoly 1832; ceded to France 1841.

polities.name: Unyanyembe
polities.note: Leading Nyamwezi ntemi chiefdom, host of the Arab caravan base at Tabora; Isike resisted Germany until 1893.

polities.name: Urambo
polities.note: Mirambo's ruga-ruga state controlling the Tabora-Ujiji route (height 1871-1884); fragmented after his death 1884.

polities.name: Nyamwezi chiefdoms
polities.note: Some 150 ntemi chiefdoms of western Tanzania; Unyanyembe and Urambo listed separately and should draw on top.

polities.name: Sukuma chiefdoms
polities.note: Many ntemi chiefdoms south of Lake Victoria.

polities.name: Kimbu chiefdoms
polities.note: Small chiefdoms in the miombo woodland between Nyamwezi and Hehe; overrun by Nyungu ya Mawe (1870s-1884).

polities.name: Hehe Kingdom
polities.note: Unified by Munyigumba, expanded by Mkwawa (r.1879-1898), who defeated the Germans at Lugalo 1891; Kalenga fell 1894.

polities.name: Sangu chiefdom
polities.note: Merere's chiefdom on the Usangu plains, Hehe rival.

polities.name: Bena chiefdoms
polities.note: Southern highland chiefdoms, partly under Hehe 1870s-1890s.

polities.name: Gogo chiefdoms
polities.note: Small pastoral chiefdoms that levied hongo tolls on the central caravan route.

polities.name: Chagga states
polities.note: Some 30 mangi chiefdoms on Kilimanjaro's southern slopes; hegemony rotated (Machame 18th c., Kibosho/Sina and Moshi/Rindi-Mandara in the 19th c.); German control 1890s.

polities.name: Kibosho
polities.note: Strongest Chagga state under Mangi Sina (c.1870-1891).

polities.name: Moshi chiefdom
polities.note: Mangi Rindi (Mandara)'s chiefdom, diplomatically prominent 1860s-1891.

polities.name: Shambaa Kingdom
polities.note: Kilindi dynasty in the Usambara mountains; height under Kimweri ye Nyumbai (c.1815-1862, reaching the coast at Tanga), then civil war; German rule 1890s.

polities.name: Ugweno
polities.note: Shana dynasty state in the North Pare mountains, fragmented in the 18th-19th c.

polities.name: Zigua
polities.note: Chiefdoms of the coastal hinterland behind Pangani; Bwana Heri's Saadani resisted Germany 1889.

polities.name: Zaramo
polities.note: Hinterland of Dar es Salaam/Bagamoyo; pazi chiefs controlled caravan tolls.

polities.name: Nyakyusa chiefdoms
polities.note: Small age-village chiefdoms north of Lake Nyasa; includes the Kyungu kingdom of Ngonde (Karonga).

polities.name: Fipa kingdoms
polities.note: Twa/Milansi and Nkansi dynasties on the Fipa plateau.

polities.name: Songea Ngoni
polities.note: Two Ngoni (Maseko/Gwangwara) states around Songea founded after migrations from the south; crushed after Maji Maji 1905-06.

polities.name: Maravi (Kalonga)
polities.note: Phiri-clan paramountcy southwest of Lake Malawi; at its height under Kalonga Masula (c.1600-1650) Maravi influence reached the Zambezi and the Mozambique coast. Declined to a local chieftaincy in the 18th c.

polities.name: Undi kingdom
polities.note: Western Maravi offshoot (Chewa) in eastern Zambia/Tete; gold trade with the Portuguese; weakened by Ngoni (Mpezeni) after 1870.

polities.name: Lundu kingdom
polities.note: Southern Maravi (Manganja) kingdom of the Shire valley; launched the Zimba invasions of the 1590s; fragmented by Kololo and Yao in the 19th c.

polities.name: Kasungu (Mwase)
polities.note: Chewa chiefdom that resisted Ngoni raids.

polities.name: Chikulamayembe
polities.note: Trader-founded Tumbuka state in northern Malawi; overrun by Mbelwa's Ngoni c.1855.

polities.name: Mbelwa's Ngoni
polities.note: Zwangendaba's successor state on the Mzimba plateau; accepted British rule 1904.

polities.name: Mpezeni's Ngoni
polities.note: Jere Ngoni state in eastern Zambia, conquered by the BSAC 1898.

polities.name: Maseko Ngoni
polities.note: Maseko Ngoni kingdom of Chikusi/Gomani in the Kirk Range; British 1896.

polities.name: Yao chiefdoms
polities.note: Ivory and slave-trading Yao chiefdoms of the Niassa highlands; migrated into southern Malawi 1850-1870. Larger chiefdoms listed separately.

polities.name: Mataka chiefdom
polities.note: Largest Yao chiefdom (Mataka I Nyambi), Niassa province; Portuguese conquest 1912.

polities.name: Mponda chiefdom
polities.note: Yao chiefdom at the southern end of Lake Malawi; British 1891.

polities.name: Makanjila chiefdom
polities.note: Yao lakeshore slave-trading chiefdom with dhow fleet.

polities.name: Massangano
polities.note: Afro-Portuguese aringa state of the Da Cruz family (Bonga) at the Luenha-Zambezi confluence; repulsed several Portuguese expeditions until 1888.

polities.name: Makanga
polities.note: Pereira family prazo-state north of Tete.

polities.name: Massingire
polities.note: Afro-Portuguese chikunda state on the lower Shire; rising 1884.

polities.name: Gorongosa (Sousa)
aliases: Manica e Sofala domain of Manuel António de Sousa
polities.note: Goan-Portuguese warlord domain controlling Gorongosa and Barwe.

polities.name: Kingdom of Zimbabwe
polities.note: Plateau state centred on Great Zimbabwe; abandoned c.1450, succeeded by Mutapa (north) and Torwa (southwest).

polities.name: Kingdom of Mutapa
polities.note: Northern Shona state on the Zambezi escarpment; at height c.1480-1500 claimed lands to the coast (Uteve, Manyika, Barwe as tributaries). Portuguese vassalage 1629; lost the plateau to the Rozvi 1690s. A rump in Chidima/Dande survived to 1917.

polities.name: Chidima Mutapa
polities.note: Successor Mutapa line in the Zambezi valley under Portuguese influence; last ruler Chioco killed 1917.

polities.name: Torwa dynasty
polities.note: Southwestern Shona successor of Great Zimbabwe; capital Khami, later Danangombe; overthrown by Changamire Dombo 1683.

polities.name: Rozvi Empire
polities.note: Changamire Dombo expelled the Portuguese from the plateau 1693-95; capitals Danangombe and Naletale. Shattered by Nguni invasions 1830s; remnants absorbed by Ndebele (last Mambo killed 1866).

polities.name: Kingdom of Manyika
polities.note: Eastern Shona gold kingdom under the Mutasa dynasty; partitioned between British and Portuguese 1891.

polities.name: Kingdom of Barwe
polities.note: Shona Tonga kingdom ruled by the Makombe; Sousa occupied it 1880-1891; finally conquered by Portugal 1902 (revolt 1917).

polities.name: Kingdom of Uteve
polities.note: Shona kingdom between Manyika and the Sofala coast; under Gaza overlordship from the 1830s.

polities.name: Kingdom of Madanda
polities.note: Small Shona-Ndau kingdom south of Uteve; under Gaza in the 19th c.

polities.name: Gaza Empire
polities.note: Founded by Soshangane after the Ndwandwe defeat; capitals Chaimite, Mossurize (Chirinda highlands, under Mzila) and Mandlakazi (Ngungunhane from 1889). Defeated by Portugal at Coolela/Chaimite 1895.

polities.name: Barotse Kingdom

overlord.name: British South Africa Company / Northern Rhodesia

polities.note: Luyana kingdom of the upper Zambezi floodplain under the Litunga; under Kololo rule 1840-1864; BSAC protectorate 1890/1900.

polities.name: Kololo kingdom
polities.note: Sotho conquest state of Sebetwane over Bulozi and the Chobe; overthrown by a Lozi rising 1864.

polities.name: Ndwandwe kingdom
polities.note: Zwide's Nguni kingdom on the Pongola-Mkuze; broken by Shaka at the Mhlatuze 1819, offshoots founded Gaza, Songea and Jere Ngoni states; remnant destroyed 1826.

polities.name: Mthethwa Paramountcy
polities.note: Dingiswayo's confederacy (Zulu were vassals); collapsed after his death 1818, absorbed by Shaka.

polities.name: Qwabe chiefdom
polities.note: Senior Nguni chiefdom absorbed by the Zulu 1818.

polities.name: Zulu Kingdom
polities.note: Shaka (KwaBulawayo), Dingane (uMgungundlovu), Mpande, Cetshwayo (Ulundi). Lands south of the Thukela lost to Natal after 1838-40. Anglo-Zulu War 1879; partitioned into 13 chiefdoms; annexed to Natal 1897.

polities.name: Kingdom of Eswatini
polities.note: Dlamini kingdom (Ngwane III, Sobhuza I, Mswati II); Mswati II's raiding reach extended north into the eastern Transvaal (c.1840-1868). ZAR protectorate 1894, British 1903.

polities.name: Mabhudu-Tembe
polities.note: Tsonga kingdom south of Delagoa Bay controlling its trade; partitioned Anglo-Portuguese 1895.

polities.name: Hlubi chiefdom
polities.note: Nguni chiefdom scattered by Mfecane 1819; later Langalibalele's location in Natal (1849-1873).

polities.name: Ngwane (Matiwane)
polities.note: Matiwane's Ngwane, migratory during the Mfecane; destroyed at Mbholompo 1828.

polities.name: Basotho Kingdom
polities.note: Moshoeshoe I's kingdom built from Mfecane refugees; lost the lowlands west of the Caledon to the Orange Free State (wars 1858, 1865-68); British protectorate (Basutoland) 1868.

polities.name: Batlokwa
polities.note: MaNthatisi and Sekonyela's Tlokwa on the upper Caledon; defeated by Moshoeshoe 1853.

polities.name: Mthwakazi
polities.note: Mzilikazi's state, on the highveld (ekuPumuleni, Mosega, eGabeni) 1827-1837, then on the Zimbabwe plateau from 1838-40; Lobengula; destroyed by the BSAC 1893.

polities.name: Maroteng Pedi kingdom
polities.note: Maroteng paramountcy (Thulare, Sekwati, Sekhukhune) between the Olifants and Steelpoort; conquered by British/Swazi force 1879.

polities.name: Venda kingdom
polities.note: Singo dynasty of the Soutpansberg (capital Dzata); later split among chiefdoms (Makhado, Mphephu); conquered by the ZAR 1898.

polities.name: Lobedu
polities.note: Sacred queenship (Modjadji) from c.1800 in the Molototsi valley.

polities.name: Ndzundza Ndebele
polities.note: Southern Ndebele kingdom of Nyabela; defeated by the ZAR in the Mapoch war 1882-83.

polities.name: Bangwato
polities.note: Largest Tswana state (Sekgoma I, Khama III); capital Shoshong, Palapye 1889, Serowe 1902. British Bechuanaland Protectorate 1885.

polities.name: Bakwena
polities.note: Senior Tswana chiefdom (Sechele, Livingstone's convert); seats Dithubaruba, Kolobeng, Dimawe, Molepolole.

polities.name: Bangwaketse
polities.note: Southern Tswana chiefdom (Makaba II, Gaseitsiwe, Bathoen).

polities.name: Batawana
polities.note: Ngwato offshoot ruling the Okavango-Lake Ngami region over Yei, Mbukushu and San.

polities.name: Bakgatla baga Kgafela
polities.note: Tswana chiefdom at Saulspoort (Transvaal) moving to Mochudi 1871.

polities.name: Barolong
polities.note: Rolong chiefdoms (Ratshidi at Mafikeng/Lotlhakane under Montshiwa; Seleka at Thaba Nchu 1833-1884). Tribal lands split by the ZAR-British border.

polities.name: Bahurutshe
polities.note: Senior Tswana chiefdom with stone-walled capital Kaditshwene (c.15-20,000 people 1820); scattered by the Mfecane.

polities.name: Batlhaping
polities.note: Southern Tswana chiefdom (Mothibi, Jantjie, Mankurwane); annexed to British Bechuanaland 1885, Cape 1895.

polities.name: Xhosa kingdom
polities.note: Tshawe-led Xhosa paramountcy; split under Phalo (d.1775) into Gcaleka and Rharhabe houses.

polities.name: Gcaleka Xhosa
polities.note: Senior Xhosa house east of the Kei (Hintsa, Sarhili); cattle-killing 1856-57; annexed after the 9th Frontier War 1878.

polities.name: Rharhabe Xhosa
polities.note: Junior Xhosa house west of the Kei (Ngqika, Maqoma, Sandile); lands annexed as Queen Adelaide Province 1835 and British Kaffraria 1847; incorporated by 1878.

polities.name: Thembu kingdom
polities.note: Cape Nguni kingdom (Ngubengcuka, Dalindyebo); annexed to the Cape 1885.

polities.name: Mpondo kingdom
polities.note: Faku's kingdom between the Mthatha and Mtamvuna; split East/West Pondoland 1840s; last independent Nguni polity annexed to the Cape 1894.

polities.name: Mpondomise
polities.note: Cape Nguni chiefdom; rebellion and annexation 1880.

polities.name: Bhaca
polities.note: Madzikane's Mfecane-era chiefdom.

polities.name: Cochoqua
polities.note: Largest Cape Khoikhoi chiefdom (Oedasoa, Gonnema); destroyed by VOC wars 1673-77 and smallpox 1713.

polities.name: Chainouqua
polities.note: Cape Khoikhoi chiefdom east of the Hottentots Holland.

polities.name: Hessequa
polities.note: Khoikhoi pastoral chiefdom, cattle trade with VOC.

polities.name: Attaqua and Outeniqua
polities.note: Southern Cape Khoikhoi groups.

polities.name: Inqua
polities.note: Powerful inland Khoikhoi chiefdom (Hykon) of the late 17th c.

polities.name: Gonaqua
polities.note: Eastern Khoikhoi, heavily intermixed with Xhosa (Gqunukhwebe).

polities.name: Little Namaqua
polities.note: Nama pastoralists south of the Orange; Leliefontein and Steinkopf reserves after 1810s.

polities.name: Korana
polities.note: Khoikhoi/Oorlam raiding groups along the middle Orange and Vaal; defeated in Korana wars 1868-1879.

polities.name: Griqualand West
polities.note: Griqua captaincy (Barends, Waterboer) at Klaarwater/Griquatown; diamond fields annexed by Britain 1871.

polities.name: Philippolis Griqua
polities.note: Adam Kok II/III's captaincy north of the Orange; sold out and trekked to Griqualand East 1861-62.

polities.name: Griqualand East
polities.note: Adam Kok III's Griqua republic; annexed to the Cape 1874/1879.

polities.name: Cape Colony
polities.note: VOC colony 1652-1795/1803-06; Batavian Republic 1803-06; British from 1806. Frontier advanced from Cape Peninsula to the Fish River (1778) and Orange/Kei (1847-1885).

polities.name: Natalia Republic
polities.note: Voortrekker republic after Blood River; annexed by Britain 1843.

polities.name: Colony of Natal
polities.note: British colony between the Thukela/Buffalo and Mtamvuna; Zululand added 1897.

polities.name: Orange Free State
polities.note: Boer republic between Orange and Vaal (preceded by British Orange River Sovereignty 1848-54); gained Caledon lowlands from Basotho 1866-69; annexed by Britain 1900/02.

polities.name: South African Republic
polities.note: Boer republic recognised at the Sand River Convention 1852; capital Potchefstroom then Pretoria (1860); British annexation 1877-81; effective control of the north (Venda, Pedi) only from 1880s-1898.

polities.name: Lydenburg Republic
polities.note: Breakaway Boer republic, reunited with the ZAR 1860.

polities.name: Zoutpansberg Republic
polities.note: Northern Boer settlement district/republic; Schoemansdal abandoned 1867 under Venda pressure.

polities.name: Republic of Utrecht
polities.note: Small Boer republic merged with Lydenburg then ZAR.

polities.name: Nieuwe Republiek
polities.note: Boer republic carved from Zululand for helping Dinuzulu; merged into ZAR 1888.

polities.name: Klein Vrystaat
polities.note: Tiny Boer republic on Swazi land; absorbed by ZAR 1891.

polities.name: Stellaland
polities.note: Boer freebooter republic on Tlhaping land; annexed into British Bechuanaland 1885.

polities.name: Land Goshen
polities.note: Boer republic on Rolong land near Mafikeng; dissolved by the Warren Expedition 1885.

polities.name: Herero chiefdoms
polities.note: Herero chiefships under paramounts Tjamuaha, Maharero, Samuel Maharero (Okahandja); German protectorate 1885; genocide 1904-08.

polities.name: Nama chiefdoms
polities.note: Khoikhoi clans of Great Namaqualand (Bondelswarts at Warmbad, Veldskoendraers, Topnaar, Rooi Nasie at Hoachanas) joined in the 19th c. by Oorlam groups (Afrikaners, Witbooi, Bethanie). Witbooi and Afrikaner listed separately.

polities.name: Orlam Afrikaners
polities.note: Oorlam captaincy of Jager and Jonker Afrikaner dominating central Namibia and the Herero 1840-1861; defeated by the Herero 1880.

polities.name: Witbooi Nama
polities.note: Oorlam Nama captaincy (Kido and Hendrik Witbooi); German treaty 1894; rising 1904-05.

polities.name: Rehoboth Basters
polities.note: Self-governing Baster community; German protection treaty 1885.

polities.name: Ondonga
polities.note: Largest Ovambo kingdom south of the Kunene floodplain; Finnish mission 1870.

polities.name: Uukwanyama
polities.note: Most populous Ovambo kingdom, straddling the Angola-Namibia border; King Mandume fell fighting Portugal/South Africa 1917.

polities.name: German South West Africa
polities.note: German protectorate; until c.1894 effective control limited to Lüderitz, Windhoek and the coast, with Herero, Nama and Ovambo polities autonomous (listed separately). Walvis Bay enclave was British/Cape.

polities.name: Kingdom of Imerina
polities.note: Andriamanelo (c.1540); seat at Antananarivo from Andrianjaka (c.1610). Imerina split into four rival kingdoms c.1710-1787; reunified by Andrianampoinimerina (Ambohimanga). As the Kingdom of Madagascar (Radama I, 1817) it conquered the east coast, Betsileo, Boina and the Antanosy south, but never Menabe, Mahafaly, Antandroy or most Bara. French conquest 1895, abolished 1897.

polities.name: Betsileo kingdoms
polities.note: Four main highland kingdoms (Lalangina, Isandra, Arindrano, Manandriana) south of Imerina; Lalangina strongest under Andriamanalina (late 18th c.). Conquered by Merina c.1815-1830.

polities.name: Lalangina
polities.note: Principal Betsileo kingdom east of Fianarantsoa.

polities.name: Isandra
polities.note: Betsileo kingdom west of Fianarantsoa (Andriamanalina I).

polities.name: Sakalava Menabe
polities.note: Maroserana-dynasty Sakalava kingdom (Andriandahifotsy) on the west coast; tributary to the Merina briefly 1820s-30s but largely independent until French rule 1890s. Fiherenana/Masikoro to the south were related.

polities.name: Sakalava Boina
polities.note: Northern Sakalava kingdom founded by Andriamandisoarivo; wealthy from Mahajanga's Indian Ocean trade; under queens from 1780s; conquered by Merina 1824-1840 (rump on Nosy Be under French 1840).

polities.name: Betsimisaraka Confederation
polities.note: Confederation of the east coast founded by the zana-malata Ratsimilaho; fragmented after 1791; absorbed by Radama I 1817 (Tamatave).

polities.name: Antemoro
polities.note: Matitana river kingdom ruled by Islamized Anteony clans with sorabe Arabic-script scholars (ombiasa); Merina garrison from 1820s.

polities.name: Antanosy
polities.note: Zafiraminia-ruled kingdom in the far southeast; French East India Company fort 1643-1674; Merina garrison 1825.

polities.name: Bara kingdoms
polities.note: Pastoral kingdoms (Bara Be, Bara Iantsantsa, Bara Imamono) of the southern plateau under Zafimanely rulers; largely independent of Merina.

polities.name: Mahafaly kingdoms
polities.note: Several Maroserana-dynasty kingdoms of the southwest plateau (Menarandra-Onilahy).

polities.name: Antandroy
polities.note: Clan-based pastoralists of the arid far south; Zafimanara chiefs; French pacification 1900-1904.

polities.name: Antankarana
polities.note: Zafimbolamena (Sakalava-derived) kingdom of the far north; King Tsimiaro sheltered on Nosy Mitsio and signed with France 1841; Merina held Diego Suarez region 1820s-1890s.

polities.name: Sihanaka
polities.note: Lake Alaotra chiefdoms conquered by Radama I 1823.

polities.name: Bezanozano
polities.note: Forest-escarpment chiefdoms between Imerina and the east coast.

polities.name: Tanala of Ikongo
polities.note: Forest people whose Ikongo plateau fortress resisted Merina conquest.

polities.name: Antaisaka
polities.note: Zarabehava-led southeast coast chiefdoms (Mananara river).

polities.name: Antambahoaka
polities.note: Small southeast coast kingdom related to the Antemoro.

polities.name: Isle de France
polities.note: Dutch posts 1638-1710; French 1715-1810; British Mauritius 1810-1968.

polities.name: Île Bourbon
polities.note: French colony (Bourbon), British occupation 1810-1815.

gaps.note: After Ajuran collapse: Ogaden, Marehan and Rahanweyn clans plus Bardera jihadist community (1819-1843); Luuq trade town. No single polity; Geledi and Ogaden clans cover the edges.
Northern Afar (Biru/Girrifo) petty sultanates and salt-trading clans; sparsely governed salt desert. Aussa and Rahayta cover the south and east.

gaps.area: Zande/Bahr el Ghazal ironstone plateau and Equatoria
gaps.note: Azande kingdoms (Avongara) and Bongo/Moru/Bari peoples; likely covered by the Central Africa file. Ivory/slave zariba states of Zubayr (1856-1874) here.
San (Basarwa) foraging bands; no polity. Tswana and Tawana claimed parts after 1800.
Uninhabited or Topnaar/Strandloper use only; Walvis Bay (Cape/British 1878).

gaps.area: Great Karoo, Bushmanland, Upper Karoo (Cape interior)
gaps.note: San hunter-gatherers and roaming Khoikhoi/Korana; no state until the Cape frontier advanced (trekboers 1740-1800).
Sotho-Tswana chiefdoms (Fokeng, Kwena, Kgatla, Taung, Tlokwa) poorly documented before 1800 and much depopulated during the Mfecane 1820-1836; Basotho, Ndebele and Boer states cover 1830s onward.
Many small Nguni chiefdoms (Qwabe, Mthethwa, Ndwandwe, Hlubi, Chunu, Thembu of Natal) without large paramountcies; only the bigger ones are itemised.
Tonga (Bitonga), Chopi and Tsonga chiefdoms (Inhambane, Zavala, Mpfumo, Nyaka at Delagoa Bay) before the Gaza conquest; poorly documented.

gaps.area: Zambia south and central (Tonga, Ila, Lenje plateau; Bemba and Kazembe further north)
gaps.note: Acephalous Tonga/Ila; Bemba/Lunda (Kazembe) kingdoms likely in the Central Africa file. Barotse and Ngoni listed here.
After the Rozvi collapse: independent Shona chiefdoms (Mashayamombe, Chivi, Makoni, Mutoko, Nyandoro), many paying tribute to Ndebele or Gaza. Zambezi valley Tonga acephalous.
Gabra, Rendille, Boran and Somali pastoralists; no states (Borana Oromo and Samburu cover edges).
Hamar, Mursi, Dassanetch, Nyangatom acephalous pastoral groups; Ethiopian raids from 1897.

gaps.area: Southern Tanzania woodlands (Selous, Ngindo, Matumbi, Mwera)
gaps.note: Thinly settled; small clan chiefdoms, Ngoni raiding after 1850. Yao and Makonde cover the south edge.
Nyamwezi/Sukuma ntemi chiefdoms emerging; little documented until 18th c. Default to the chiefdom confederations listed.
Small Sakalava-related Fiherenana kingdoms around Toliara; partly covered by Menabe and Mahafaly.
Before the Maroserana and Merina dynasties: small Vazimba/clan chiefdoms; Islamic trading posts at Mahilaka/Vohemar (Antalaotra). Leave uncoloured or low-confidence.
